_comments.source: Hand-curated 2026-04-05. Deliberately off-distribution: medication-managed chronic condition, not procedural. Stress-tests whether the procedure-volume-based pipeline architecture generalizes.
_comments.hcpcs_rationale: HTN care is overwhelmingly E&M-visit-driven. 99202-99215 are new/established outpatient visits. 93784/93786/93788/93790 cover ambulatory BP monitoring (recording, scanning, analysis, review). 93000/93005/93010 ECGs are routine workup. 80053/80061/82947/83036/81003 are standard labs (CMP, lipid, glucose, HbA1c, UA) for end-organ/secondary-cause evaluation. Note: E&M codes are ubiquitous across nearly all physicians, so this set is low-specificity by design — that is the finding this condition is meant to surface.
_comments.taxonomy_rationale: Primary care (Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, General Practice) manages most HTN. Cardiology, Nephrology, and Endocrinology handle resistant/secondary cases.
_comments.pubmed_rationale: Management, guideline, and specific-variant queries (resistant, renovascular, secondary). ABPM is included as a workup modality.
